profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point in Siena, Italy, tagged telecom=data_center, is named E. D. Accounting Siena. The word "Accounting" in the business name plainly identifies this as an accounting or bookkeeping practice serving local clients, not a data center or IT hosting business. Accounting firms maintain their own office computing and, in many cases, client financial-record servers, but that is a fundamentally different function from a commercial colocation or cloud data center. The telecom=data_center tag on this point is best explained as a mapping error applied to the firm's own small server room or network closet, and this entry records that determination plainly rather than inventing data-center specifications for an accounting office.

reading.body:
A point in Siena, Italy, tagged as a data center is an accounting firm, so any facility count drawn from this source carries at least one false positive.

The name itself says so. E. D. Accounting Siena is identified by the word "Accounting" as a bookkeeping practice, and the record's own reading concludes the telecom=data_center tag is a mapping error applied to the firm's own server room or network closet. Supporting fields are consistent with that: no operator, no website, and zero megawatts. An accounting office runs office computers and may keep client financial records on a local machine. That is not colocation and not cloud hosting.

This matters for AI because counting data centers is the first step in counting compute, and compute is what the buildings and the power connections exist to serve. A bookkeeping office's file server sits in the same category as a hyperscale campus under a tag like this one, and the two are not comparable in load, in cooling, or in grid demand. The error here is small in capacity terms, since nothing is recorded, but it is a category error rather than a rounding error.

What this does not establish is how often the same mistake occurs elsewhere. One reviewed point says nothing about the accuracy of the wider inventory, nothing about Italy's actual data center capacity, and nothing about the grid. No operator, no capacity figure, and no power connection is recorded for this site, so no conclusion about Siena's real compute footprint can be drawn from it.
